This analysis is partially confirmed by the possible source - a lifting filament seen in STEREO A EUV 304 close to the west limb as seen from STEREO A (close to 159 degrees).
Somewhat speculative analysis based on SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and on the very approximate location of the AR rotating onto the visible disk and seen on/behind the east limb in SDO AIA 193/304.

Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2.

In STEREO A COR2, there is a faint leading edge observed already far in the east field-of-view after a data gap ends at 2026-09-24T01:23Z that better corresponds to te eruption time, but also plausible to match this leading edge.
GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 triangulation, full width and leading edge somewhat obscured by this front's overlap with the preceeding streamer blowout.

Very speculative analysis based on the location of the possible source (a faint filament eruption seen in STEREO A EUV 195) and on the front seen only in one coronagraph (STEREO A COR2) since the CME is not seen in other coronagraphs.

Slow, narrow feature first seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2. Is it only seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and fades before leaving the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2. The source is possibly related to some rising filamentary structures best seen in GOES SUVI 304. This activity begins several hours prior to the CME start time and persists after.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to single coronagraph view and on/beyond limb source candidate.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the WSW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-09-12T08:38Z. This feature is only seen in STEREO A COR2. No good source candidate can be seen in SDO AIA or STA EUVI, so the source is most likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen do to single coronagraph viewpoint and lack of source candidate.

data.note: CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-09-13T01:24Z. It is also seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C3. This CME is mostly obscured by Earthshine in GOES CCOR-1 and is not seen in STEREO A COR2. There is no definitive source candidate, but the source may be related to some minor activity in a filament structure over the W limb best seen in GOES SUVI 304 beginning around 2026-09-13T22:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to single coronagraph view and uncertain, near-limb source candidate.

data.note: Very narrow CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-09-13T07:48Z. It is first seen part way into the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2 and is also seen in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but not in STEREO A COR2. The source may be related to minor field line movement beyond the SW limb best seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-09-13T06:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to beyond-limb source and lack of triangulation.

data.note: CME first seen to the W in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-09-13T10:23Z and fades before leaving the FOV of STEREO A COR2. This feature is not see in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or in GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely related to field line movement seen beyond the WNW limb in STA EUVI 195 beginning after 2026-09-13T08:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to single coronagraph view and beyond-limb source.

data.note: CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-13T19:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-09-13T19:23Z. The source of this event is a center disk filament eruption beginning at approx. 2026-09-13T18:48Z best seen in SDO AIA and STEREO A COR2 304, centered at approx. S10W10. This filament appears to be deflected towards the NW, which is supported by dimming seen moving towards the NW, expanding to approx. N10W30 as seen in SDO AIA 193. This eruption is close to a large coronal hole which may contribute to the deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: BULK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-09-13T21:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-09-13T19:23Z. The source of this CME is likely outflow following an earlier filament eruption beginning at 2026-09-13T18:48Z centered at approx. S10W10 as seen in SDO AIA 193 and 304. This CME is likely deflected to the NW due to proximity to a large coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME first seen to the E in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-09-14T11:08Z. It is also seen to the W in GOES CCOR-1. This CME is covered by a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real time. The source of this CME is an eruption centered around AR 14528 (S11W38) best seen in GOES SUVI 284 beginning around 2026-09-14T10:00Z. Field line movement can be seen accompanied by brightening and ejecta. Post-eruptive arcades can also be seen in SDO AIA 193. There seems to be a northwestward deflection from the location of the source. There are two large coronal holes (a northern and a southern one) nearby, possibly responsible for this deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit of the brighter, likely bulk, front following the fainter shock in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit of the faint earliest front in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, likely not observed in STEREO A COR2 either due to faintness or a data gap starting at 2026-09-14T18:53Z before it becomes visible. The source is far-sided over the NW limb, observed in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-09-17T15:48Z as slow, wide field line movement. More directly observed in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 starting as early as 2026-09-14T14:55Z, as brightening and dimming centered around an estimated N30W115 in the NW disk near former Active Regions 14523 and 14521.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only 3D analysis, using W115 as the approximate observed source in STEREO A EUVI, as STEREO A COR2 does not observe the CME in real-time for triangulation.

data.note: Very faint CME with an unclear front seen to the NE in early images of SOHO LASCO C2 only. It is not seen in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1, likely because of its faintness. No source for this feature has been found in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is also faintly visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 following a data gap due to Earthshine from 2026-09-18T03:45Z to 2026-09-18T06:10Z. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is beyond the NE limb and is seen as moving field lines starting at 2026-09-18T02:35Z in GOES SUVI 284 and SDO AIA 171/193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement based on SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: Faint, narrow CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 and very faintly seen in a couple of frames of GOES CCOR-1 coronagraph imagery. The CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO C3. Its source is likely seen in STEREO A EUV 304 imagery as a large ejecta off the W limb after 2026-09-19T15Z and not seen in any other EUV imagery. The ejecta is not clearly visible, and it's exact location/longitude is unclear, but it seems to be close to the limb (which would be ~159 deg).

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based exclusively on the fit of the narrow front in two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2); longitude of 143 deg seems to be the highest longitude allowing the fit. This analysis is partially confirmed by the possible source - a lifting filament seen in STEREO A EUV 304 close to the west limb as seen from STEREO A (close to 159 degrees).

data.note: Faint, minor CME with an unclear front seen to the E-NE in SOHO LASCO C2. Not seen in other coronagraphs. Its source is the long duration C3.3 class flare from unnumbered AR rotating onto disk (N14E90) peaking at 2026-09-19T18:17Z. There is also an associated opening of field lines on/behind the E limb seen in SDO AIA 193 and a minor prominence/ejecta seen in SDO AIA 304/171 starting after 2026-09-19T18:10Z. The initial front is followed by a series of outflows.

cmeAnalyses.note: Somewhat speculative analysis based on SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and on the very approximate location of the AR rotating onto the visible disk and seen on/behind the east limb in SDO AIA 193/304.

data.note: CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is a far-sided filament eruption over the NW limb, observed best in GOES 284/304 starting around 2026-09-19T21:22Z. When STEREO A EUVI 304/195 return from a data gap at 2026-09-20T00:15Z and 2026-09-20T00:25 respectively, dimming and post eruptive brightening can be seen in the NW disk, likely left behind by this filament eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The front appears more wide in COR2 than C3, as such COR2's width is used.

data.note: CME observed brightly to the SW in STEREO A COR2, and very faintly to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. No source is seen in on-disk EUV imagery for this event, and is likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, better seen the further into the field-of-view it travels than early C2. No definitive EUV source is observed, and may be far-sided or outflow following prior CME: 2026-09-19T18:48Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C3 only plane-of-sky.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2. No distinct source is observed for this CME, but could be related to field line movement over the NW limb starting as early as ~2026-09-20T01:48Z in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 plane-of-sky. The CME is less than 10 half-width and deflected northward, making it difficult to track the proper CME front travel with swpc_cat.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the W only in STEREO A COR2. No distinct source is observed in available EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 plane-of-sky taken at W159.6, with STEREO A located at W69.9.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 (may be too faint) or GOES CCOR-1 (likely pylon obscured). No distinct EUV source is observed for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 plane-of-sky.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3, not in GOES CCOR-1 as it is likely obscured by the pylon. The only potential source is a slow brightening on the NW disk of STEREO A EUVI 195 starting around 2026-09-20T18:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2, very faint in LASCO but trackable.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3, largely blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source is unclear, with a potential far-sided source on the STEREO A EUVI 195/304 west limb observed as brightening and field line movement starting around 2026-09-21T09:05Z, very close to the CME start time however. There are two additional field line movements near the NW limb in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2026-09-21T03:03Z and 2026-09-21T05:54Z, however these eruptions may be too early to be associated with this CME. Triangulation of the leading edge suggests the CME is far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME observed to the E only in STEREO A COR2, likely not seen in other coronagraphs due to the occulting disk and/or faint leading edge. The start time of 2026-09-24T02:53Z in white light is later than the first observation at 2026-09-24T01:38Z in running difference imagery due to the bright streamer overlap. The source may be an eruption from AR 14536 centered around N03W32, observed as slow dimming, brightening, and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-09-23T21:06Z. In STEREO A COR2, there is a faint leading edge observed already far in the east field-of-view after a data gap ends at 2026-09-24T01:23Z that better corresponds to this eruption time, but is also plausible to be a candidate source for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only analysis using the source N03W32 as a basis, as such the parameters could vary. In STEREO A COR2, there is a faint leading edge observed already far in the east field-of-view after a data gap ends at 2026-09-24T01:23Z that better corresponds to te eruption time, but also plausible to match this leading edge.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SW only in STEREO A COR2, may be due to faintness or the occulting disk in other coronagraphs. No EUV source is observed for this front.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 plane-of-sky given the unknown, likely far-sided, source; taken at W159.8 with STEREO A currently at W69.8.

data.note: CME observed to the SW in GOES CCOR-1 and S in STEREO A COR2, overlapping with a slow, wide streamer blowout beginning ~2026-09-23T20:12Z (itself measuring ~176 km/s). Not observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a real-time data gap. The source is field line movement and small shifting of a coronal hole boundary best observed only in GOES SUVI 284 starting ~2026-09-24T14:02Z, tracing on-disk around S35W70 in proximity to a large southern coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 triangulation, full width and leading edge somewhat obscured by this front's overlap with the preceeding streamer blowout.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME is also visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source is farsided, and is best seen as rapidly opening field lines beyond the west limb in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting at 2026-09-25T10:25Z. Moving field lines are also visible beyond the east limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the wider, fainter, shock feature of the CME based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Updated measurement of the leading edge based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2, GOES CCOR-1, and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Preliminarily measurement of the leading edge of the CME based on limited available GOES CCOR-1, SOHO LASCO C2, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Narrow CME with a pointy front seen in STEREO A COR2 only. This CME partially overlaps in coronagraphs with the far-sided 2026-09-25T11:09Z CME and its shock. The only potential candidate source is a filament liftoff faintly seen to the south in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting 2026-09-25T11Z as a faint dimming and faint post-eruptive arcades centered ~S40W80 or W90. Not really seen in GOES SUVI 304 or STEREO A 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very speculative analysis based on the location of the possible source (a faint filament eruption seen in STEREO A EUV 195) and on the front seen only in one coronagraph (STEREO A COR2) since the CME is not seen in other coronagraphs.

data.note: Faint loop front in the wake of 2026-09-25T11:09Z CME, overlapping with outflow from this earlier far-sided CME. The front is faintly seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 to the NE. There is a super faint, possibly corresponding front even more faintly seen in STEREO A COR2 white light imagery to the NW but it is practically not seen in running difference imagery and seems much wider than the front seen in LASCO and CCOR-1. No source has been found in available EUV imagery for this event, so it is likely far sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: The super faint possible front seen in STEREO A COR2 to the NW does not fit with the clearer fronts seen in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1. No source has been found for this CME in EUV imagery. Only POS analysis is possible for this event

data.note: Faint CME that looks to consist of two imperfect loops moving together as one. It is seen faintly to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C3 difference imagery, moving in the footsteps of 2026-09-25T11:09Z CME. No coronal signatures have been found for this event, so it is likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: The faint front is only seen in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 and not seen in STEREO A COR2. No source has been found for this CME in EUV imagery. Only POS analysis is possible for this event.

data.note: A minor narrow CME seen to the E in GOES CCOR-1/SOHO LASCO C3. It is not seen in STEREO A COR2. No coronal signatures have been found for this CME in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME was not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery and no source has been found for it in EUV imagery, therefore only POS analysis is possible for it.

data.note: A narrow CME seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1/SOHO LASCO C3 with a pointed front. It is not seen in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2 currently because of a data gap. No coronal signatures have been found for this CME in EUV imagery, except for possibly some movement of field lines to the NE seen in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME has not been seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery and no definitive source has been found for it in EUV imagery, therefore only POS analysis is possible.

data.note: The flare was produce by the unnumbered Active Region just behind the limb. This is likely the Active Region that would be numbered AR 14535.
